sanskrit: dvijottamaiḥ sarvagatair abhiṣṭuto; vidīptatejā gatamanyur īśvaraḥ praśāntacetā muditaḥ svam ālayaṃ; triviṣṭapaṃ prāpya mumoda vāsavaḥ
english: Praised by the foremost of the twice-born who were gathered from everywhere, his splendor blazing forth, his wrath now gone, the lord with a tranquil heart and gladdened, having reached his own abode, the heaven of the gods—Vāsava rejoiced.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pūrvarūpāṇi me rājan puruṣasya bhaviṣyataḥ parābhaviṣyataś caiva tvaṃ me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O king, tell me, grandsire, of the foretokens of a man who is about to rise and of one who is about to fall.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mana eva manuṣyasya pūrvarūpāṇi śaṃsati bhaviṣyataś ca bhadraṃ te tathaiva nabhaviṣyataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: It is the mind itself, blessings upon you, that proclaims a man's foretokens—both of the one who will prosper and of the one who will not.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam śriyā śakrasya saṃvādaṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this they recount an ancient tale, the colloquy of Śrī with Śakra. Mark it well, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: mahatas tapaso vyuṣṭyā paśyaṃl lokau parāvarau sāmānyam ṛṣibhir gatvā brahmalokanivāsibhiḥ
english: By the fruit of great austerity he beheld both worlds, the higher and the lower, having attained fellowship with the seers who dwell in Brahmā's realm—

sanskrit: brahmaivāmitadīptaujāḥ śāntapāpmā mahātapāḥ vicacāra yathākāmaṃ triṣu lokeṣu nāradaḥ
english: that very Brahman-like Nārada, of boundless blazing might, his sins stilled, great in austerity, roamed at will through the three worlds.

sanskrit: kadā cit prātar utthāya pispṛkṣuḥ salilaṃ śuci dhruvadvārabhavāṃ gaṅgāṃ jagāmāvatatāra ca
english: Once, rising at dawn and wishing to touch the pure water, he went to the Gaṅgā that issues from the Gate of Dhruva, and stepped down into her.

sanskrit: sahasranayanaś cāpi vajrī śambarapākahā tasyā devarṣijuṣṭāyās tīram abhyājagāma ha
english: And the thousand-eyed wielder of the thunderbolt, slayer of Śambara and Pāka, came likewise to the bank of that river frequented by the divine seers.

sanskrit: tāv āplutya yatātmānau kṛtajapyau samāsatuḥ nadyāḥ pulinam āsādya sūkṣmakāñcanavālukam
english: The two, self-controlled, having bathed and finished their prayers, sat down together, reaching a sandbank of the river spread with fine golden sand.

sanskrit: puṇyakarmabhir ākhyātā devarṣikathitāḥ kathāḥ cakratus tau kathāśīlau śucisaṃhṛṣṭamānasau pūrvavṛttavyapetāni kathayantau samāhitau
english: Fond of converse, with minds pure and gladdened, the two recited tales told by holy doers and recounted by the divine seers, intent and discoursing of things long past and gone.

sanskrit: atha bhāskaram udyantaṃ raśmijālapuraskṛtam pūrṇamaṇḍalam ālokya tāv utthāyopatasthatuḥ
english: Then, beholding the rising sun heralded by its net of rays, its orb made full, the two rose and stood in worship before it.

sanskrit: abhitas tūdayantaṃ tam arkam arkam ivāparam ākāśe dadṛśe jyotir udyatārciḥsamaprabham
english: And close beside that rising sun, like a second sun, there appeared in the sky a radiance whose splendor matched flames leaping upward.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samīpaṃ saṃprāptaṃ pratyadṛśyata bhārata tat suparṇārkacaritam āsthitaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ padam bhābhir apratimaṃ bhāti trailokyam avabhāsayat
english: It was seen drawing near to the two, O Bhārata: it had reached the Vaiṣṇava station traversed by Garuḍa and the sun, and shone with peerless rays, illumining the three worlds.

sanskrit: divyābhirūpaśobhābhir apsarobhiḥ puraskṛtām bṛhatīm aṃśumatprakhyāṃ bṛhadbhānor ivārciṣam
english: Attended by celestial nymphs of surpassing form and grace, she was vast and sunlike in brilliance, like the flame of the mighty-rayed luminary—

sanskrit: nakṣatrakalpābharaṇāṃ tārābhaktisamasrajam śriyaṃ dadṛśatuḥ padmāṃ sākṣāt padmatalasthitām
english: her ornaments arranged like constellations, her garland patterned like the spangling of stars—Śrī, the lotus goddess, they beheld in person, standing upon a lotus-pedestal.

sanskrit: sāvaruhya vimānāgrād aṅganānām anuttamā abhyagacchat trilokeśaṃ śakraṃ carṣiṃ ca nāradam
english: That peerless among women descended from the front of her aerial car and approached Śakra, lord of the three worlds, and the seer Nārada.

sanskrit: nāradānugataḥ sākṣān maghavāṃs tām upāgamat kṛtāñjalipuṭo devīṃ nivedyātmānam ātmanā
english: Maghavan, with Nārada following him, came up to her in person and, with palms joined in salute, presented himself before the goddess.

sanskrit: cakre cānupamāṃ pūjāṃ tasyāś cāpi sa sarvavit devarājaḥ śriyaṃ rājan vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: And that all-knowing king of the gods rendered her unmatched homage, O king, and to Śrī he spoke these words.

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ kena ca kāryeṇa saṃprāptā cāruhāsini kutaś cāgamyate subhru gantavyaṃ kva ca te śubhe
english: Who are you, O sweetly-smiling one, and on what errand have you come? Whence do you arrive, fair-browed one, and whither must you go, O auspicious lady?

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca puṇyeṣu triṣu lokeṣu sarve sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ mamātmabhāvam icchanto yatante paramātmanā
english: Śrī said: Throughout the three holy worlds all beings, moving and unmoving, desiring to make me their own, strive with their utmost selves.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ vai paṅkaje jātā sūryaraśmivibodhite bhūtyarthaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ padmā śrīḥ padmamālinī
english: I am she who was born in the lotus awakened by the sun's rays—Padmā, Śrī, garlanded with lotuses, born for the prosperity of all beings.

sanskrit: ahaṃ lakṣmīr ahaṃ bhūtiḥ śrīś cāhaṃ balasūdana ahaṃ śraddhā ca medhā ca sannatir vijitiḥ sthitiḥ
english: I am Lakṣmī, I am Prosperity, and I am Śrī, O slayer of Bala; I am Faith and Wisdom, Modesty, Conquest, and Constancy.

sanskrit: ahaṃ dhṛtir ahaṃ siddhir ahaṃ tviḍ bhūtir eva ca ahaṃ svāhā svadhā caiva saṃstutir niyatiḥ kṛtiḥ
english: I am Fortitude, I am Success, I am Radiance and Affluence too; I am Svāhā and Svadhā, Praise, Necessity, and Action.

sanskrit: rājñāṃ vijayamānānāṃ senāgreṣu dhvajeṣu ca nivāse dharmaśīlānāṃ viṣayeṣu pureṣu ca
english: In the vanguards and the banners of kings who go forth to victory, in the dwellings of those of righteous conduct, in their realms and their cities—

sanskrit: jitakāśini śūre ca saṃgrāmeṣv anivartini nivasāmi manuṣyendre sadaiva balasūdana
english: in the lord of men who bears the splendor of conquest, who is valiant and never turns back in battles—there do I forever dwell, O slayer of Bala.

sanskrit: dharmanitye mahābuddhau brahmaṇye satyavādini praśrite dānaśīle ca sadaiva nivasāmy aham
english: In him who is ever devoted to dharma, of great understanding, friendly to brahmins, truthful in speech, humble, and inclined to giving—there do I always dwell.

sanskrit: asureṣv avasaṃ pūrvaṃ satyadharmanibandhanā viparītāṃs tu tān buddhvā tvayi vāsam arocayam
english: Once I dwelt among the Asuras, bound to them by their truth and righteousness; but when I knew them turned to their opposites, I resolved to dwell with you.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca kathaṃvṛtteṣu daityeṣu tvam avātsīr varānane dṛṣṭvā ca kim ihāgās tvaṃ hitvā daiteyadānavān
english: Śakra said: When the Daityas behaved in what manner did you dwell among them, O fair-faced one? And seeing what here did you come, forsaking the sons of Diti and the Dānavas?

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca svadharmam anutiṣṭhatsu dhairyād acaliteṣu ca svargamārgābhirāmeṣu sattveṣu niratā hy aham
english: Śrī said: I take my delight in beings who keep to their own duty, who do not waver from steadfastness, who find their joy in the path to heaven.

sanskrit: dānādhyayanayajñejyā gurudaivatapūjanam viprāṇām atithīnāṃ ca teṣāṃ nityam avartata
english: Among them there ever prevailed giving, study, sacrifice and worship, reverence for elders and gods, and honor shown to brahmins and to guests.

sanskrit: susaṃmṛṣṭagṛhāś cāsañ jitastrīkā hutāgnayaḥ guruśuśrūṣavo dāntā brahmaṇyāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: Their houses were well-swept, their womenfolk well-governed, their fires duly offered; they were attentive to their teachers, self-restrained, devoted to brahmins, and truthful.

sanskrit: śraddadhānā jitakrodhā dānaśīlānasūyakāḥ bhṛtaputrā bhṛtāmātyā bhṛtadārā hy anīrṣavaḥ
english: Faithful, masters of their anger, generous, free from spite, they maintained their sons, their counselors, and their wives, and harbored no envy.

sanskrit: amarṣaṇā na cānyonyaṃ spṛhayanti kadā cana na ca jātūpatapyante dhīrāḥ parasamṛddhibhiḥ
english: Free from rancor, they never coveted one another's goods, and being steadfast, they were never once tormented by the prosperity of others.

sanskrit: dātāraḥ saṃgṛhītāra āryāḥ karuṇavedinaḥ mahāprasādā ṛjavo dṛḍhabhaktā jitendriyāḥ
english: Givers and gatherers alike, noble, knowing compassion, of great graciousness, upright, firm in devotion, their senses subdued—

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭabhṛtyasacivāḥ kṛtajñāḥ priyavādinaḥ yathārthamānārthakarā hrīniṣedhā yatavratāḥ
english: their servants and ministers content, themselves grateful and sweet of speech, bestowing honor and wealth according to merit, restrained by modesty, firm in their vows.

sanskrit: nityaṃ parvasu susnātāḥ svanuliptāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ upavāsatapaḥśīlāḥ pratītā brahmavādinaḥ
english: On the holy days they bathed well, anointed and adorned themselves; given to fasting and austerity, of good repute, expounders of the sacred word.

sanskrit: nainān abhyudiyāt sūryo na cāpy āsan prageniśāḥ rātrau dadhi ca saktūṃś ca nityam eva vyavarjayan
english: The sun never rose upon them still asleep, nor were they wakeful through the night; and at night they ever shunned curds and parched-grain meal.

sanskrit: kālyaṃ ghṛtaṃ cānvavekṣan prayatā brahmacāriṇaḥ maṅgalān api cāpaśyan brāhmaṇāṃś cāpy apūjayan
english: At dawn the pure and continent ones would look upon clarified butter; they gazed too upon auspicious things and gave honor to the brahmins.

sanskrit: sadā hi dadatāṃ dharmaḥ sadā cāpratigṛhṇatām ardhaṃ ca rātryāḥ svapatāṃ divā cāsvapatāṃ tathā
english: Theirs ever was the dharma of those who give and never accept, who sleep for half the night and stay awake by day.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇānāthavṛddhānāṃ durbalāturayoṣitām dāyaṃ ca saṃvibhāgaṃ ca nityam evānumodatām
english: They took constant pleasure in giving and sharing with the wretched, the helpless, the aged, the weak, the sick, and women.

sanskrit: viṣaṇṇaṃ trastam udvignaṃ bhayārtaṃ vyādhipīḍitam hṛtasvaṃ vyasanārtaṃ ca nityam āśvāsayanti te
english: The dejected, the frightened, the agitated, the terror-stricken, the disease-afflicted, the man robbed of his wealth, the calamity-stricken—these they ever consoled.

sanskrit: dharmam evānvavartanta na hiṃsanti parasparam anukūlāś ca kāryeṣu guruvṛddhopasevinaḥ
english: They followed only dharma and did each other no harm; obliging in their dealings, they waited upon their elders and teachers.

sanskrit: pitṛdevātithīṃś caiva yathāvat te 'bhyapūjayan avaśeṣāṇi cāśnanti nityaṃ satyataporatāḥ
english: They duly honored the ancestors, the gods, and their guests, and ate only what was left over, ever devoted to truth and austerity.

sanskrit: naike 'śnanti susaṃpannaṃ na gacchanti parastriyam sarvabhūteṣv avartanta yathātmani dayāṃ prati
english: None ate alone of a well-furnished meal, nor went to another's wife; toward all beings they bore the same compassion as toward themselves.

sanskrit: naivākāśe na paśuṣu nāyonau na ca parvasu indriyasya visargaṃ te 'rocayanta kadā cana
english: Never in the open air, nor with beasts, nor in what is no fit womb, nor on the holy days, did they ever consent to the release of their seed.

sanskrit: nityaṃ dānaṃ tathā dākṣyam ārjavaṃ caiva nityadā utsāhaś cānahaṃkāraḥ paramaṃ sauhṛdaṃ kṣamā
english: Ever present in them were giving and skill, uprightness always, energy and freedom from egotism, the highest friendliness, and forbearance.

sanskrit: satyaṃ dānaṃ tapaḥ śaucaṃ kāruṇyaṃ vāg aniṣṭhurā mitreṣu cānabhidrohaḥ sarvaṃ teṣv abhavat prabho
english: Truth, giving, austerity, purity, compassion, gentle speech, and no treachery toward friends—all this dwelt in them, O lord.

sanskrit: nidrā tandrīr asaṃprītir asūyā cānavekṣitā aratiś ca viṣādaś ca na spṛhā cāviśanta tān
english: Drowsiness, sloth, ill-will, unguarded envy, discontent, despondency, and craving never entered them.

sanskrit: sāham evaṃguṇeṣv eva dānaveṣv avasaṃ purā prajāsargam upādāya naikaṃ yugaviparyayam
english: It was among the Dānavas, while they bore such virtues, that I once dwelt of old, from the time of creation, through more than one turning of the ages.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālaviparyāse teṣāṃ guṇaviparyayāt apaśyaṃ vigataṃ dharmaṃ kāmakrodhavaśātmanām
english: Then, in the turning of time, as their virtues were turned about, I saw dharma departed from them, who had become slaves to desire and wrath.

sanskrit: sabhāsadāṃ te vṛddhānāṃ satyāḥ kathayatāṃ kathāḥ prāhasann abhyasūyaṃś ca sarvavṛddhān guṇāvarāḥ
english: When the elders among the assembly told their true tales, those of lesser worth laughed at them and reviled all their elders.

sanskrit: yūnaḥ sahasamāsīnān vṛddhān abhigatān sataḥ nābhyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ yathāpūrvam apūjayan
english: When the worthy aged came and sat among the young, the young no longer honored them, as once they had, by rising and saluting.

sanskrit: vartayanty eva pitari putrāḥ prabhavatā ''tmanaḥ amitrabhṛtyatāṃ prāpya khyāpayanto 'napatrapāḥ
english: Even while the father still lived and held sway over himself, the sons took over the running of affairs, reducing him to the state of an enemy's servant and proclaiming it shamelessly.

sanskrit: tathā dharmād apetena karmaṇā garhitena ye mahataḥ prāpnuvanty arthāṃs teṣv eṣām abhavat spṛhā
english: And for those who, by deeds blameworthy and gone from dharma, won great wealth—for such men did their craving grow.

sanskrit: ucchaiś cāpy avadan rātrau nīcais tatrāgnir ajvalat putrāḥ pitṝn abhyavadan bhāryāś cābhyavadan patīn
english: They spoke loudly even by night, while there the fire burned low; sons spoke back to their fathers, and wives answered back their husbands.

sanskrit: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ vṛddham ācāryam atithiṃ gurum guruvan nābhyanandanta kumārān nānvapālayan
english: Mother, aged father, preceptor, guest, and elder—they no longer welcomed as elders deserve, nor did they look after their children.

sanskrit: bhikṣāṃ balim adattvā ca svayam annāni bhuñjate aniṣṭvā saṃvibhajyātha pitṛdevātithīn gurūn
english: Without giving alms or offering oblation, they ate the food themselves, without first making the sacrifice or sharing with ancestors, gods, guests, and elders.

sanskrit: na śaucam anurudhyanta teṣāṃ sūdajanās tathā manasā karmaṇā vācā bhaktam āsīd anāvṛtam
english: Their cooks no longer observed cleanliness, in thought, deed, or word; the food was left uncovered.

sanskrit: viprakīrṇāni dhānyāni kākamūṣakabhojanam apāvṛtaṃ payo 'tiṣṭhad ucchiṣṭāś cāspṛśan ghṛtam
english: The grains lay scattered, food for crows and mice; the milk stood uncovered, and persons defiled by their leavings touched the clarified butter.

sanskrit: kuddālapāṭīpiṭakaṃ prakīrṇaṃ kāṃsyabhājanam dravyopakaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ nānvavaikṣat kuṭumbinī
english: The hoe, the basket, the bronze vessel lay strewn about; the mistress of the house no longer kept watch over the goods and the implements at all.

sanskrit: prākārāgāravidhvaṃsān na sma te pratikurvate nādriyante paśūn baddhvā yavasenodakena ca
english: They did not repair the breaches in their walls and houses, nor did they trouble, having tethered their cattle, to tend them with fodder and water.

sanskrit: bālānāṃ prekṣamāṇānāṃ svayaṃ bhakṣān abhakṣayan tathā bhṛtyajanaṃ sarvaṃ paryaśnanti ca dānavāḥ
english: Before the very eyes of their watching children they ate the dainties themselves, and so the Dānavas devoured all that belonged to their dependents.

sanskrit: pāyasaṃ kṛsaraṃ māṃsam apūpān atha śaṣkulīḥ apācayann ātmano 'rthe vṛthāmāṃsāny abhakṣayan
english: Milk-rice, the dish of rice and sesame, meat, cakes, and wafers they cooked for their own sake, and ate meat killed to no sacred purpose.

sanskrit: utsūryaśāyinaś cāsan sarve cāsan prageniśāḥ avartan kalahāś cātra divārātraṃ gṛhe gṛhe
english: They lay asleep past sunrise, and all stayed wakeful through the night; quarrels went on there, day and night, in house after house.

sanskrit: anāryāś cāryam āsīnaṃ paryupāsan na tatra ha āśramasthān vikarmasthāḥ pradviṣanti parasparam saṃkarāś cāpy avartanta na ca śaucam avartata
english: The ignoble there no longer waited upon a noble man as he sat; doers of forbidden deeds hated those settled in the proper stages of life, and one another; confusion of castes prevailed, and purity prevailed no more.

sanskrit: ye ca vedavido viprā vispaṣṭam anṛcaś ca ye nirantaraviśeṣās te bahumānāvamānayoḥ
english: Brahmins learned in the Veda and those plainly ignorant of the hymns were treated with no distinction between them, in honor or in contempt.

sanskrit: hāvam ābharaṇaṃ veṣaṃ gatiṃ sthitim avekṣitum asevanta bhujiṣyā vai durjanācaritaṃ vidhim
english: To observe their coquetry, their ornament and dress, their gait and their bearing, their servant-maids cultivated the ways of wicked folk.

sanskrit: striyaḥ puruṣaveṣeṇa puṃsaḥ strīveṣadhāriṇaḥ krīḍārativihāreṣu parāṃ mudam avāpnuvan
english: Women in the garb of men, and men wearing the garb of women, found their highest delight in games, dalliance, and revels.

sanskrit: prabhavadbhiḥ purā dāyān arhebhyaḥ pratipāditān nābhyavartanta nāstikyād vartantaḥ saṃbhaveṣv api
english: The gifts once bestowed by men of power upon the worthy they no longer honored, out of unbelief, though they had the means to do so.

sanskrit: mitreṇābhyarthitaṃ mitram arthe saṃśayite kva cit vālakoṭyagramātreṇa svārthenāghnata tad vasu
english: When a friend besought a friend in some doubtful matter of wealth, the latter, for a self-interest no greater than the tip of a hair's end, would cheat him of that wealth.

sanskrit: parasvādānarucayo vipaṇyavyavahāriṇaḥ adṛśyantāryavarṇeṣu śūdrāś cāpi tapodhanāḥ
english: Eager to seize the goods of others, dealing in trade and barter, men of the noble orders came to be seen as Śūdras—while Śūdras, on the other hand, were rich in austerity.

sanskrit: adhīyante 'vratāḥ ke cid vṛthāvratam athāpare aśuśrūṣur guroḥ śiṣyaḥ kaś cic chiṣyasakho guruḥ
english: Some studied without keeping their vows, others kept their vows to no purpose; a pupil there was who would not serve his teacher, and a teacher who made a comrade of his pupil.

sanskrit: pitā caiva janitrī ca śrāntau vṛttotsavāv iva aprabhutve sthitau vṛddhāv annaṃ prārthayataḥ sutān
english: Father and mother both, worn out as though their feast of life were ended, the aged pair, stripped of all authority, begged their food of their own sons.

sanskrit: tatra vedavidaḥ prājñā gāmbhīrye sāgaropamāḥ kṛṣyādiṣv abhavan saktā mūrkhāḥ śrāddhāny abhuñjata
english: There the wise, learned in the Veda, ocean-like in their depth, became absorbed in farming and the like, while fools ate the funeral offerings.

sanskrit: prātaḥ prātaś ca supraśnaṃ kalpanaṃ preṣaṇakriyāḥ śiṣyānuprahitās tasminn akurvan guravaś ca ha
english: Morning after morning the courteous greeting, the dressing of hair, and the errands that pupils once performed—in that age it was the teachers who did them, sent at the pupils' bidding.

sanskrit: śvaśrūśvaśurayor agre vadhūḥ preṣyān aśāsata anvaśāsac ca bhartāraṃ samāhūyābhijalpatī
english: In the very presence of her father- and mother-in-law the young wife gave orders to the servants, and summoning her husband, scolded and ordered him about.

sanskrit: prayatnenāpi cārakṣac cittaṃ putrasya vai pitā vyabhajaṃś cāpi saṃrambhād duḥkhavāsaṃ tathāvasan
english: With all his effort the father guarded the favor of his son's mind; and they divided the patrimony in fury, and so dwelt in a wretched dwelling.

sanskrit: agnidāhena corair vā rājabhir vā hṛtaṃ dhanam dṛṣṭvā dveṣāt prāhasanta suhṛtsaṃbhāvitā hy api
english: When they saw a man's wealth consumed by fire, or carried off by thieves or by kings, they laughed out of malice—though they had once been counted his well-wishers.

sanskrit: kṛtaghnā nāstikāḥ pāpā gurudārābhimarśinaḥ abhakṣyabhakṣaṇaratā nirmaryādā hatatviṣaḥ
english: Ungrateful, unbelieving, wicked, defilers of their teachers' wives, given to eating what should not be eaten, knowing no bounds, their luster slain—

sanskrit: teṣv evamādīn ācārān ācaratsu viparyaye nāhaṃ devendra vatsyāmi dānaveṣv iti me matiḥ
english: when they practiced such ways and worse in this perversion, I would no longer dwell among the Dānavas, O lord of the gods—such was my resolve.
